concepts.name: Cape of Good Hope vs Cape Agulhas: Southernmost Point of Africa
key_dimensions: Common misconception: Cape of Good Hope is NOT the southernmost tip of Africa — Cape Agulhas is
Cape Agulhas as the official boundary between Atlantic and Indian Oceans
Strategic maritime significance of Cape of Good Hope for historical trade routes (spice route)
Location in South Africa and proximity to each other causing frequent confusion

concepts.name: Cape Horn: Southernmost Tip of South America
key_dimensions: Located on Hornos Island, Chile — NOT on the mainland of South America (island trap)
Marks the boundary between Atlantic and Pacific Oceans in the southern hemisphere
Distinction from Strait of Magellan as an alternative route around South America
Drake Passage lies between Cape Horn and Antarctica — strategic geopolitical significance

concepts.name: Arabian Peninsula: Largest Peninsula in the World
key_dimensions: Bounded by Red Sea (west), Arabian Sea (south), Persian/Arabian Gulf (northeast) — exact boundary identification
Countries entirely within the peninsula: Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Oman, UAE, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait
Geopolitical significance: OPEC dominance, Strait of Hormuz proximity
Comparison with Indian subcontinent peninsula in terms of area and geopolitical framing

concepts.name: Indian Peninsula: Deccan Plateau and Southern Tip
key_dimensions: Cape Comorin (Kanyakumari) as the southernmost tip of the Indian mainland — distinction from southernmost point of India (Indira Point, Andaman & Nicobar)
Three water bodies meeting at Kanyakumari: Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea, Indian Ocean
Indian peninsula bounded by Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats converging at Nilgiris
UPSC trap: Southernmost point of India vs southernmost point of Indian mainland

concepts.name: Indira Point: Southernmost Point of India
key_dimensions: Located on Great Nicobar Island, Andaman & Nicobar Islands — NOT on the Indian mainland
Submerged partially during 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami — disaster geography angle
Proximity to Indonesia's Sumatra island — strategic maritime boundary significance
Distinction from Kanyakumari (Cape Comorin) — a frequent UPSC trap

concepts.name: Scandinavian Peninsula: Northernmost Capes of Europe
key_dimensions: North Cape (Nordkapp) in Norway — commonly cited as northernmost point of Europe (but technically Knivskjellodden is further north)
Cape Nordkinn as the northernmost point of the European mainland (another trap layer)
Scandinavian Peninsula encompasses Norway, Sweden, and part of Finland
Strategic Arctic Council relevance and Northern Sea Route geopolitics

concepts.name: Iberian Peninsula: Westernmost Point of Continental Europe
key_dimensions: Cape Roca (Cabo da Roca), Portugal — westernmost point of continental Europe
Bounded by Atlantic Ocean (west/south) and Mediterranean Sea (east) — Strait of Gibraltar at southeast
Countries: Spain and Portugal — with Andorra as a landlocked microstate within
Historical significance: Gateway for Age of Exploration voyages

concepts.name: Cape Chelyuskin and Northernmost Points of Continental Asia
key_dimensions: Cape Chelyuskin in Russia — northernmost point of the Asian continent and of the Eurasian landmass
Located on Taymyr Peninsula, Siberia — Arctic Ocean proximity
Northern Sea Route strategic importance connecting Europe and Asia
Distinction: Northernmost point of Asia vs northernmost point of Russia vs northernmost point of Europe

concepts.name: Korean Peninsula: Geopolitical and Geographic Significance
key_dimensions: Bounded by Yellow Sea (west), Sea of Japan/East Sea (east), Korea Strait (south)
38th Parallel as the de facto boundary between North and South Korea — DMZ significance
Strategic chokepoint between China, Japan, and Russia — relevance to Indo-Pacific geopolitics
Cape relevance: Southernmost tip near Busan — Korea Strait connecting Yellow Sea and Sea of Japan

concepts.name: Malay Peninsula and Cape Piai: Southernmost Point of Continental Asia
key_dimensions: Tanjung Piai (Cape Piai), Malaysia — southernmost point of continental Asia
Strait of Malacca runs along the western side — world's busiest maritime chokepoint
Peninsula shared between Thailand, Malaysia, and a tiny part of Myanmar
Distinction from Singapore, which is an island just off the peninsula's tip

concepts.name: Cape Verde and Cape Verde Islands: Westernmost Point of Africa
key_dimensions: Cape Verde (Cabo Verde) on the Senegal coast — westernmost point of the African continent
Distinction from the Cape Verde Islands (an island nation in the Atlantic) — a classic UPSC trap
Cape Verde Islands: Volcanic archipelago, Portuguese-speaking, significant for Atlantic navigation history
Dakar, Senegal's capital, located near Cape Verde — geographic proximity significance

concepts.name: Cape Guardafui: Horn of Africa
key_dimensions: Located in Somalia — northeasternmost point of Africa, forming the 'Horn of Africa'
Strategically located at the Gulf of Aden meeting the Indian Ocean — Somali piracy and naval patrols
Horn of Africa countries: Somalia, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Djibouti — geopolitical and humanitarian significance
Proximity to Bab-el-Mandeb strait — critical chokepoint for Red Sea trade

concepts.name: Kamchatka Peninsula: Easternmost Peninsula of Asia
key_dimensions: Located in Far East Russia, between Sea of Okhotsk (west) and Pacific Ocean/Bering Sea (east)
Part of Pacific Ring of Fire — high volcanic and seismic activity
Cape Dezhnev (not on Kamchatka but in Chukotka) — easternmost point of Asia and Russia, nearest to Alaska across Bering Strait
Strategic military significance during Cold War — Russian Pacific Fleet and submarine bases

concepts.name: Baja California Peninsula: Gulf of California Formation
key_dimensions: Located in Mexico — separates the Gulf of California (Sea of Cortez) from the Pacific Ocean
One of the longest peninsulas in the world by length
Unique biodiversity hotspot — UNESCO World Heritage marine area in Gulf of California
Distinction between Baja California (state) and Baja California Sur (state) — administrative trap

concepts.name: Florida Peninsula and Cape Canaveral: Strategic US Geography
key_dimensions: Florida Peninsula separates the Gulf of Mexico from the Atlantic Ocean
Cape Canaveral — NASA's Kennedy Space Center, historical and current space launch significance
Straits of Florida between Florida and Cuba — strategic maritime passage
Florida Keys extension southward — proximity to Cuba and Caribbean geopolitics

concepts.name: Sinai Peninsula: Africa-Asia Land Bridge
key_dimensions: Only land connection between Africa and Asia — between Gulf of Suez (west) and Gulf of Aqaba (east)
Politically part of Egypt (Africa) but geographically considered a bridge to Asia
Suez Canal cuts through Egypt west of Sinai — making Sinai technically an 'island' between canal and Red Sea arms
Geopolitical significance: Arab-Israeli conflicts, Suez Crisis, current security (ISIS affiliates)

concepts.name: Antarctic Peninsula: Northernmost Extension of Antarctica
key_dimensions: Northernmost part of Antarctica, pointing toward South America — closest point to Drake Passage
Most contested region under Antarctic Treaty System — overlapping territorial claims by Argentina, Chile, and UK
Fastest warming region on Earth — climate change and glacier retreat indicator
India's research stations context: Maitri and Bharati located in other parts of Antarctica (not the Peninsula)

concepts.name: Cape Farvel (Farewell): Southernmost Tip of Greenland
key_dimensions: Cape Farewell (Nunap Isua) — southernmost point of Greenland and of the North American tectonic plate broadly
Greenland's strategic significance: Arctic Council, US interest in purchasing Greenland (2019 controversy)
Greenland as world's largest island — distinction from Australia (continent) and Arabian Peninsula (largest peninsula)
Denmark–Greenland autonomous relationship — relevant for Arctic geopolitics questions

concepts.name: Crimean Peninsula: Black Sea Geopolitics
key_dimensions: Located between Black Sea and Sea of Azov — annexed by Russia from Ukraine in 2014
Kerch Strait connects Black Sea and Sea of Azov — strategic chokepoint controlled post-annexation
Sevastopol as Russia's key warm-water naval base for Black Sea Fleet
Current relevance: Russia-Ukraine War, NATO Black Sea dynamics, grain export disruptions

concepts.name: Cape Bojador and Historical Navigation Significance
key_dimensions: Located on the coast of Western Sahara (Morocco-administered) — long considered an impassable barrier in medieval European navigation
Gil Eanes (Portuguese) first rounded it in 1434 — opening route for African coastal exploration
Connects to Age of Discovery narrative — Portugal's role and Prince Henry the Navigator
Western Sahara's disputed status — Morocco vs Polisario Front — current geopolitical relevance
